items.item: OpenTelemetry defines traces, metrics, logs and baggage as its signals (profiles/events still proposal-stage), and the Collector is a vendor-agnostic receive/process/export pipeline so applications export once (OTLP).

items.item: traceparent carries version-trace_id-parent_id-flags in a fixed, portable format; every compliant tool must at minimum forward it.

Messaging spans use links, not parent/child, as the default correlation because a span can have only one parent, batch fan-in has many producers, and consumption can happen inside another ambient span.
A span's link count is configurable with a default limit (128); a batch receive accounting for more messages than that drops links beyond the limit.
Kafka-specific and shared messaging semantic-convention attributes (messaging.destination.name, messaging.destination.partition.id) make a Kafka trace and a database trace queryable the same way.
Debezium supports OpenTelemetry tracing, but a CDC write is a real break point: trace metadata must be explicitly passed through it, not assumed to propagate.
OpenLineage's object model (Job, Dataset, Run, RunEvent) answers a different question than OTel: what a job read/wrote per run, not what happened during one execution.

items.item: Topic 1's correlation key (run/task/asset/partition) and golden signals are the base this topic adds a trace on top of.

Chapter 8's CDC architecture and Chapter 9's Kafka records/headers and Flink/Spark consumers are the concrete systems this topic's trace crosses — both chapters are unbuilt as of this topic's build, so their ids are declared, not used, per CHAPTER.md's cross-chapter-id rule.
A quantile/percentile, a Kafka record as carrier (queues-vs-logs), and logical decoding (CDC) are prior-chapter ideas this topic leans on without re-teaching.

The W3C Trace Context Recommendation is the standard OpenTelemetry's HTTP/Kafka-header propagation implements; a Kafka hop has no HTTP request, so the header map is carried in the record's own headers instead.
A trace and a log can be correlated by TraceId/SpanId (topic 1's forward pointer), but a trace and a lineage event share only the idea of a run identifier, not a data model.
